svg.title: O-RAN architecture and interfaces
svg.desc: SMO with rApps and Non-RT RIC (R1), O1 dashed lines from the SMO to the Near-RT RIC, O-CU-CP, O-CU-UP, O-DU, O-RU and O-eNB, A1 down to the Near-RT RIC. The O-Cloud spans an edge site hosting the Near-RT RIC, O-CU-CP and O-CU-UP, and a far-edge site hosting the O-DU, managed by the SMO over O2 through IMS and DMS. E2 from the Near-RT RIC to the CU-CP, CU-UP and DU, Y1 to external users, O1 to every managed element. E1 between CU-CP and CU-UP, F1-C and F1-U from the edge site to the far-edge site, Open Fronthaul to the physical O-RU, Uu to the UE, NG-C and NG-U to the 5G core, Xn-C and Xn-U to a neighbor gNB and X2 to an O-eNB.
svg.text: O-Cloud · one operator cloud spanning several sites
regional data center · a few ms from the radio

g.text: E2 termination · subscriptions · SDL · conflict mitigation
many xApps, often from different vendors · loops 10 ms – 1 s
RLC · MAC · High-PHY · scheduler · FEC accelerator
Training phase · offline, in the SMO and its data platform
Collect O1 PM, traces, MDT, RLF reports and exported E2 records fill the data lake
Train the trainer builds features and labels and trains models; MLflow registers the best
Deploy model and alert policy reach the Near-RT RIC over A1; the xApp is deployed over O2
Retrain outcomes and new RLF labels return over O1 for retraining and drift checks
Inference phase · online, in the Near-RT RIC every second
Ingest live E2 KPM and RC reports reach the RLF xApp every second
Score the xApp builds each UE's feature window, scores it and merges alerts into episodes
Alert alerts go to NOC dashboards and the OSS over Y1
Act optional: a pre-emptive handover or parameter change goes to the O-CU-CP over E2-RC
E2: per-UE KPIs and RRC events up, control down (primary RLF data)
O1: PM, FM, traces up, configuration down (labels, cell counters)
Other O-RAN interfaces: A1, R1, Y1, O2, Open Fronthaul
3GPP interfaces: E1, F1, NG, Xn, X2, Uu
RLF application flows; arrows show direction; T = training, I = inference
O-Cloud; thin dotted boxes are its sites
Arrowheads: two heads = traffic in both directions; one head (Y1) = one way
